A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same heterogeneous-vocabulary speculative-decoding work. Their text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison. The publication agreement appended to v2 adds no research evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding benchmarks, vocabulary-overlap measurements, tokenizer-injectivity tests, and an empirical analysis of token-decomposition complexity.

after.justification: v2 reports expanded decoding benchmarks and vocabulary-overlap measurements, while retaining the original tokenizer and token-decomposition analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix B corrects Algorithm 5, which Algorithms 1 and 4 invoke: the final token uses the residual distribution only after rejection; otherwise it is sampled directly from the target. v1 always specified residual sampling. The core SLEM, SLRS, and TLI mechanisms remain unchanged; this establishes a pseudocode correction, not an implementation change.

E1.justification: The Stack code-generation evaluation in v1 Table 7 is absent from v2. CNN-DailyMail, SCROLLS, and HumanEval remain, preserving summarization, long-context, and code-generation coverage. Added model families do not introduce new tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Autoregressive decoding and Hugging Face's standard speculative decoding remain the comparison algorithms. Both are retained in the corresponding Gemma benchmarks, and the added DeepSeek benchmarks reuse these baselines. New target and drafter choices expand model configurations rather than introduce another competing decoding method.

E3.justification: v2 substantially revises the benchmark configuration matrix, adding DeepSeek distilled targets and drafters and comparisons across GPU setups, while removing standalone Llama throughput configurations. It drops the 1e-07 temperature condition, separates SLEM at temperature zero from TLI at temperature one, and adds explicit AR-relative speedups. The 30-prompt averaging protocol remains.

E4.justification: The task-conditioned vocabulary-overlap diagnostic expands from selected pair/task examples in v1 Table 6 to comparisons across datasets and additional model pairs in v2 Table 10. The token-decomposition complexity study, Figures 1–3, and tokenizer-injectivity experiment are retained. No new component-ablation study is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions average benchmark results over 30 prompts without reporting repeated seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The descriptive statistics and density estimation for token-decomposition counts are unchanged. Additional benchmark rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive DeepSeek results and replaces many existing benchmark values. For example, Mixtral/CNN-DailyMail at temperature zero reports AR/vicuna throughput of 10.2/9.9 tokens per second in v1 Table 7 versus 7.8/16.4 in v2 Table 1. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains, because v1 omits hardware details. Phi-4/SCROLLS values are retained, while task-specific overlap results are expanded.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects standard SD's stated guarantee from identical outputs to equality in distribution and removes the assertion that its expected acceptance rate is at least that of autoregressive decoding. The named theorems, vocabulary assumptions, token-composition lemma, and proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance; appendix moves and lemma renumbering add no theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains three lossless methods requiring no additional training. v2 specifies headline speedups of up to 2.8× for SLEM and 1.7× for TLI, and drops v1's claim that TLI outperforms SLEM on average. It also adds a claim that Hugging Face maintainers found both methods most effective among previously supported speculative-decoding algorithms.

C2.justification: The limitations discussion newly identifies architecture and training differences as factors affecting acceptance rates and points to benchmark failures with insufficiently fast or accurate drafters. It replaces v1's explicit qualification about optimized homogeneous SD potentially outperforming the proposals with greater emphasis on benefits even when homogeneous alternatives exist.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a benchmarking-repository address, identifies GPU types and counts for benchmark configurations, and states a generation range of 128–512 new tokens per prompt. It also reports completed TLI integration into Transformers, which was pending in v1. These substantially expand reproducibility and access information, although the repository itself was not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references for models and datasets, including Phi, Mixtral, Vicuna, Gemma 2, CodeLlama, HumanEval, and SCROLLS. The positioning relative to prior speculative-decoding research remains largely unchanged. Publication updates and duplicate entries for existing works do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 revises the contributions, empirical-results narrative, and limitations; standardizes algorithm terminology; and reorganizes appendices into separate speedup, vocabulary, and proof sections. It also changes the author list and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Most technical exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The benchmark presentation is substantially redesigned into separate SLEM and TLI tables, with explicit method, hardware, and speedup columns and multipage appendix tables. The task-specific overlap table is greatly expanded. Figures 1–3 retain their content but move with the reorganized appendices; these are relocations, not new figures.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Algorithm 5's missing all-accepted sampling case and substantially improves experimental auditability through hardware disclosures, generation details, and a benchmark-code reference. Its broader comparisons report both speedups and slowdowns, giving a stronger basis for assessing practical applicability. Removing The Stack and near-zero-temperature results reduces coverage, and headline claims remain imperfectly synchronized with the tables, including TLI's stated 1.7× maximum versus 2.04× in Table 7. These drawbacks do not outweigh the gains in correctness and experimental transparency.
